seo_title: Delhi HC: Aadhaar Alone Can't Prove Date of Birth
title: Delhi High Court Holds Aadhaar Card Alone Cannot Prove Date of Birth, Upholds Worker's Back Wages
case_name: M/s J.J. Electronics v. Smt. Rosamma Joy
citation: W.P.(C) 16476/2022; judgment dated 13 November 2026 (Ohri, J.; reserved 14 August 2026)
card_summary: The employer had told the ESIC the worker's birth year was 1960, then later relied on a different Aadhaar date to retire her a year early. The Labour Court found the retrenchment illegal. Justice Manoj Kumar Ohri dismissed the employer's writ, holding an Aadhaar card alone cannot override the employer's own earlier record of her age, and upheld her back wages with interest.
card_tip: An employer who has already recorded an employee's date of birth with a statutory body such as the ESIC cannot later rely on a different Aadhaar date to retire that employee early.
verification_notes: The case name, writ number W.P.(C) 16476/2022, bench (Justice Manoj Kumar Ohri) and the 13 November 2026 pronouncement date are reported consistently by LiveLaw, Bar and Bench and LawChakra, each covering the ruling independently. The back-wages figure of Rs 14,698 per month for the stated period, plus 6% interest, comes from LawChakra's account of the operative order. Sources differ on the worker's actual birth date: LiveLaw and Bar and Bench describe the dispute as being between the ESIC-recorded year (1960) and a different Aadhaar year, while one other outlet gave 20 May 1959 as the Aadhaar date; the card states only the ESIC-versus-Aadhaar discrepancy on which the main reports agree and does not assert either specific date as fact.
